as discussed here are my answers for DE:

# Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied? *yes --> legal figure of pseudo self-employment*
# Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc) *No*
# Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria? *No*
# Are reclassification sensitive activity expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship? *The typical control test applies as in other markets. How much control is actually exerted on individual drivers via procedures?*
# Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings?) *Yes, for three years if the holder of the claim has knowledge or is grossly negligent in not having knowledge of the circumstances giving rise to the claim .*
# Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators *Regulator, Driver, in special cases Unions*
# Is there any evidence the authorities have considered drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities etc)? *No, only licensing is a topic at the moment.*
# What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, requirement to have a representative etc)? *Easy access to justice.*
# Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers of the platform in a market at once? *No, however, actions can be combined into one action through the figure of subjective aggregation of actions or joinder of actions. A representative action in labour law is not known to date.*

It makes a clear sense that this *Implicit expiry date rule should also reside in* {{document-auto-accept-service}} along with the rest of the rules.

Implementation options:

* Extend the existing checkers to hold the information that the expiry date is implicit. 
{noformat}if(checker.isImplicitExpiryDate()){
  rule = checker.getImplicitExpiryDateRule()
  expiryDate = deriveExpiryDate(issueDate, rule)
}{noformat}
** Extremely easy to implement. Good amount of coherency with the existing rules.
** It will need change when we decommission the class based rules.
* Create a separate config which stores the {{document_type}}, {{is_implicit_expiry_date}} and the {{rule}} . Use this config to derive the {{expiry_date}}.
** Extremely easy to implement
** This will introduce one more document based config.

I would like to go with second implementation option here as this will be required when we integrate with the new configuration based rules anyways.

Hey, Mariann! 

*In short* – discounts offered to new Bolt Market users should not be taken into account (should not factor into the formula) when calculating the 30-day-price.

The European Commission has released a notice on 29.12.2021 for the guidance on the interpretation and application of Article 6a of Directive 98/6/EC (PID) which contains the price reduction requirement. It can be found [here|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52021XC1229(06)]. It states in section 2.3 of the notice, under „Loyalty programmes and personalised price reductions“ that article 6a of the PID (i.e. the 30-day-price rule) does not apply _to personalised price reductions that are granted on special occasions for the consumer, such as signing up to the loyalty programme or on the consumer’s marriage or birthday, as well as reductions applied at the time of the purchase that have not been ´announced´ in advance._

Signing up to use Bolt Market for the first time is a personalised price reduction since the scope of people is very limited and therefore falls outside of the scope of article 6a and does not have to be taken into account when calculating the 30-day-price of a product. Of course this is my opinion and in an ideal world would be verified with the Estonian authorities, but considering that the example given in the guidance document (i.e. the “_signing up to the loyalty programme_”) is so analogous to the first time customer cohort, then the risk seems minimal.

For example: If a bag of chips is sold to a new Bolt Market user at a large discount (example 0,5 EUR), that discounted price can be left out of the calculation for the 30-day-price that is shown to the engaged users of Bolt Market. The calculation for the 30-day-price is done using prices that are not personalised offers.

----

If we have no proof of the event:

* Confirm how many previous reports of its kind we have against the reported user;
* Take the consequential action according to the Cannot Be Confirmed ([Regular Event|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3467837733/Food+HP+How-To+Ticket+and+Event+Assessment+Investigation+Reporting#Regular-Events]) table depending on the number of previous offenses;
* *Send a message informing the reported user accordingly (i.e. educate or warn the user, or send a message to the user informing them about the suspension).*

----

If we have proof of the event:

* Confirm how many previous reports of its kind we have against the reported user;
* Take the consequential action according to the Confirmed ([Regular Event|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3467837733/Food+HP+How-To+Ticket+and+Event+Assessment+Investigation+Reporting#Regular-Events]) table depending on the number of previous offenses;
* *Send a message informing the reported user accordingly (i.e. educate or warn the user, or send a message to the user informing them about the suspension).*

----

Always keeping in mind that we cannot block providers without ops consent (the tool has a reminder for this already).

Location = Location. No logic there 😄 If location is blank in Telema, no location will be displayed in Workday.

Note that the bottom logic STOPS when being read top to bottom, and it hits an ‘if’ that is *true*.

Region:

* If it is a “Rounding” line…
** Region for this line is selected as per the country of the company (eg: EE003 = Estonia)
* If a Region value is coming through from Telema, while no Location data is coming through
** Select the Region from Telema
* If Telema provides a Location, and the location is mapped against a Region on the Integration maps
** Select the Region based on the integration maps
* If Telema provides a Location *and* a Region, and the location is NOT mapped on the integration maps
** Select the Region from Telema
* If none of the above are applicable…
** Set the Region to the Dummy Region.

Let me know if there’s any questions about this logic.

K.r. Tim

[~accountid:623d9fdba2f6400069ec4d84] please see my comments: 

* From a legal point of view, Bolt is not providing the transportation service to the riders - transportation services are provided to riders by drivers/fleets (i.e. Bolt is not a party to this legal relationship). As per applicable [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-riders/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-riders/|smart-link], we are not liable for acts and omissions of the driver. Thus, if there was any damage caused to the rider during the ride, the rider should submit these claims against the driver and not against Bolt.
* However, setting aside the legal set-up, refusing the compensation could have possible negative backlash and bad customer experience. Bolt in Estonia had an incident, where the court decided that Bolt is responsible for the actions of the driver. In that case, managed to conclude a compromise, but we need to be aware of possible dangers.
* Considering the low value of the compensation and the extensive resources we would invest in case the case is escalated, we may make a kind move to pay the compensation on behalf of the driver to the granny. This decision is to be made by the CS team. 
* There is no common approach, every case needs to be assessed on the case by case basis, considering possible negative repercussions and resources we need to allocate in case of a dispute. That is, it seems cheaper to pay EUR 120 than to have a dispute.
* In case the CS team opts to pay the compensation, we shall sign the compromise/settlement agreement with the passenger, which clearly states that the payout shall remain confidential and Bolt does not have to pay anything under the law.

Our onboarding process focuses on covering general topics for agents, such as product knowledge, tools, soft skills, quality, and common CS issues. Unfortunately, we don't specifically address concrete situations like this one regarding walk-ins, as our outsourced agents are not working in such environments. Additionally, walk-ins are not available in all the cities where we operate.

Including brief information on this topic during onboarding wouldn't be worthwhile for a few reasons. Firstly, it may not align with the learning curve that agents naturally experience. Secondly, the impact of theoretical knowledge on this specific case may not be as significant as the practical experience and guidance provided by their managers and trainers. Lastly, the concept is better grasped when agents have hands-on experience rather than relying solely on theory (e.g. role-play, simulations, etc.)

Given these reasons, we recommend involving team leads or managers to ensure that necessary precautions are taken and agents are coached on how to handle such cases. If further guidance or support is required, our training team will assess the training and learning needs and prioritize them accordingly. We can also provide materials on soft skills to assist agents and managers in dealing with these or similar situations, in case we are unable to deliver specific training or lessons in the near future 🙇‍♂️.

The use case sounds legit. However, i also need to explicitly state that version of the table would not represent a state of the source database and backend system but the time when it was ingested to the lake. Since we don’t have explicit ETAs on data arrival to the lake - you can not depend on arrival time in a reliable way. There is also always a chance of outage and backfilling (in that case history would be in incorrect order within time-traveling). 

The additional thing why we feel reluctant with this request is that we perform many data changes under the hood ( eg. to improve query performance) and these changes create a new table version which we have to keep as well. That would explode our data storage costs. 

So considering all the above - our more reliable recommendation is still to use immutable replication and something like a slowly-changing-dimensions-etl on top of this approach. 

If you accepted all the drawbacks and were still fine with the time-traveling we could create a backlog ticket to allow granular adjustment of this setting and assigning explicit data owners (for cost-assigning matter).

Then we don’t see any legal issues from a consumer perspective with implementing this in Finland as we will follow the same principles as with our regular rides. As long as we stay clear with the pricing information and stick to the fixed price principle and obtain consumer consent for the fixed price then there do not seem to be any new obstacles with this features. 

However, will this feature be made available to all drivers? This is important as including a preference over certain drivers over other drivers imposes a high reclassification risk and we would therefore not be able to green-light this feature at this stage if it is only provided to certain drivers. 

Generally from a legal perspective, the option imposing the lowest reclassification risk is to offer the feature to all drivers. This option is well defendable and even strengthens our position against reclassification risks. We will be able to say that drivers who join us to deliver transportation services may choose different ways of how to provide services on our platform, meaning there is a lot of freedom for drivers as to how they choose to use our platform.

Here are the responses to *Employment law research - Saudi Arabia:*



# *Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?*

As a preliminary point, the definition of an “employer” and “worker” under the Labour Law are as follows:

# *Employer* – _Any natural or corporate person employing one or more workers for a wage_
# *Worker* - _Any natural person working for an employer and under his management or supervision for a wage, even if he is not under his direct control._

 

Further, Article 50 of the Labour Law confirms that _a work contract is a contract concluded between an employer and a worker, whereby the latter undertakes to work under the management or supervision of the former for a wage_.

# In light of the definitions described above, the KSA market is subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied, i.e. someone can be deemed to be an employee if they are working under the supervision and control of an employer in return for a wage.
# Further, the contractual relationship between drivers and "Participatory Electronic Platforms" (“*PEP*”), which is the sector that Bolt operates in, is regulated by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (“*MHRSD*”). Individuals are engaged either as service providers in their personal capacity or through a third-party entity through a B2B agreement.
# Please note that only Saudi nationals can be engaged as a driver  through direct registration on Bolt’s phone application (the “*App*”) and would be considered a service provider rather than employees of Bolt. In addition, both expatriates and Saudi nationals can also be drivers in Bolt through a third-party entity (Operating Facility) providing services to Bolt through a B2B agreement (e.g., providing Bolt with drivers to achieve 1000 deliveries per day). 

*2. Is there any evidence that platforms are under scrutiny under the legal system (litigation etc.)?*

# Yes. Employment relationships in PEP are undergoing continuous regulation and improvements through relevant authorities including the MHRSD.
# The MHRSD issued a Ministerial Resolution dated January 2021 together with a detailed guidance on PEPs. Further, the MHRSD have issued a statement confirming that it is looking to limit the exploitation of workers who violate the PEP platforms and are looking at potentially creating a national labour policy to ensure that the sector provides job opportunities for Saudi nationals.
# We  are not aware of any litigation cases related to such platforms. Further, please note that litigation cases in KSA are not published to the public as there is no concept of case reporting. Further, it is very rare for labour cases to be reported in the local press, and we are not aware of any published reports concerning litigation relating to PEPs. 



*3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?*

# Please note our comments above regarding the broad statutory definitions of employer and worker. Further, the Labour Law provides that an employment relationship can be created by a written or unwritten contract, and that the law applies on every employment contract through which an employee works for and under the employer’s administration and supervision in return for a wage.
# We understand that Bolt will not have supervision and control over the drivers as the drivers can choose when to work and have the choice of accepting or rejecting a job. Further, whilst the fare ride is collected on behalf of the drivers, we understand that Bolt issues an invoice to the drivers for its commission payment. Our view is that the drivers do not receive a wage from Bolt, but the drivers may try to  argue otherwise.
# In light of 3(a), and given that the relevant MHRSD regulations do not consider drivers as employees of the PEP, we consider the relationship between (1) a Saudi national driver directly registered with Bolt through the App and (2) Bolt as a civil contractual commercial relationship, with the drivers being service providers.
# That said, in the event of a dispute, the Courts will consider the actual relationship between the parties and how it is implemented in practice. Based on their assessment of the facts, it is possible that they could consider that the arrangement amounts to an employer and worker relationship. However, we consider this is likely to be low risk given the Ministerial Resolution and guidance issued by the MHRSD clarifying that the drivers are not employees.

 

*4. Are reclassification-sensitive activities expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

# Please note our comments above regarding the broad statutory definitions of employer and worker, and the factors that are considered when assessing whether an employment relationship exists.
# The MHRSD has jurisdiction for reclassification as regulates this area of work. Additionally, the Saudi Courts have the discretion to issue judgements which could include case to case reclassification in this regard. Please note that there is no concept of judicial precedent in KSA and courts are therefore not bound by the earlier decisions of other courts..

 

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings)?*

# Yes, if the drivers can establish that they are employees of Bolt, there is no time limit under Shari’ah law on how far back a claim for wages can be made.
# As the drivers are considered service providers and do not hold an employment relationship, they may be able to make a claim in the general court for breach of contract and have five years from the date of the breach to bring a claim.

 

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt? Drivers / group action / regulators?*

# The MHRSD and any other relevant Governmental Regulators have the discretion to impose fines if they establish that Bolt has breached any applicable laws or regulations.
# On the basis that the legal relationship between Bolt and its drivers directly who are registered through the App is likely to be considered as a civil contractual commercial relationship, drivers registered directly through the App can take action against Bolt provided they have legal basis for the claims.
# Although it is very uncommon in KSA, it is possible that a group of drivers could also submit complaints to the MHRSD which may then intervene in an attempt to resolve the dispute. This is only likely to happen if there is a large number of employees submitting a similar complaint.

 

*7. Is there any evidence that the authorities have considered Drivers eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g., tax authorities, pension authorities, etc)?*

# At present, we are not aware of the authorities considering Drivers to be eligible for employment benefits. As the PEP market is relatively new and is growing at a considerable rate, with an increasing number of Saudi nationals registering with such PEPs, we expect the position to develop and evolve over time, and it may be something that is looked at in the future.

 

*8. What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g., high state duties, the requirement to have a representative, etc.)?*

# Justice in KSA generally is highly accessible to all employees through the Labour Court and service providers through the General Court.
# In the Labour Court, no legal representative is required for the amicable resolution stage, but the Respondent must have a legal representative before the Labour Court.
# Further, there are no judicial fees payable for submitting a claim in the Labour Court, and it is generally very rare for costs awards to be made against claimants.

 

*9. Can claims be made to reclassify all Drivers of the platform in a market at once?*

# Yes, the MHRSD can receive general claims including claims to reclassify directly registered drivers in Bolt from service providers to employees. However, the MHRSD has the sole discretion of deciding whether there are grounds for the claims, and whether it will act upon the claims.

The advice received for *Sweden* is as set out below. As you can see they also added a brief reclassification review and as we already know we can’t make an assessment solely based on the stickets but would need to conduct an overall review of the circumstances. This is however a separate topic from the marketing law assessment but I still wanted to include it in the ticket for reference. 

+Swedish marketing law assessment+:

A trader may not use inaccurate claims or other presentations in the marketing which are misleading with respect to the commercial operations of the trader or a third party. According to Swedish case law, a company is free to refer to different types of cooperations with other companies. However, this must not be done in such a way as to mislead consumers as to the nature, scope, or relevance of the collaboration in the context at hand.

Bearing in mind the set-up of the Bolt ride-hailing vertical, the driver being connected to the Bolt app and the terms thereof as set out in the terms and conditions between the driver and Bolt, our assessment is that *such stickers would not result in misleading marketing or otherwise constitute a breach of Swedish marketing law*.

+Swedish employment law assessment:+

From a Swedish employment perspective, it can be noted that the distinction between employees, on the one hand, and independent contractors (i.e. consultants, self-employed etc.), on the other hand, is usually determined based on an overall assessment of all circumstances in each individual case.

One of the indicators of an employment relationship, according to case law, could be that that the individual appears (from an outside perspective) to be an employee of the company. Using a Bolt sticker could therefore potentially have relevance when assessing the risk for reclassification. However, as previously mentioned, an overall assessment shall be made, and it would also be relevant to assess the agreement between the parties in general, taking into account e.g. the scope and extent of the engagement, the consultant's tax status, the consultant's independence in terms of e.g. working tools, performance of the work, etc. As such, it seems unlikely that the Bolt sticker would – solely on its own – be decisive when determining whether the individual should be classified as an employee or not.

There are no specific Norwegian requirements regarding campaigns and advertisements in the form of car-branding. The general rules in the Norwegian Marketing Control Act (“MCA”) applies, e.g. the campaigns and advertisements on the cars must not conflict with good marketing practice, the marketing must be designed and presented in such a way that it is clear that it is marketing, and the marketing cannot contain false or misleading information.

There is thus *no strict legal requirement* provide additional information in connection with having a Bolt logo on the car.

Having said that, a driver is not necessarily driving exclusively for Bolt (i.e one may “risk” entering a car believing it is a “Bolt car” while the driver is actually driving for another provider) – especially if it is possible to just stop a car on the street as opposed to book through the app in advance,  there is also in Norway a potential risk that the “Bolt logo” on the car could be deemed misleading if the driver is in fact are driving with another provider. But also this risk in our view vests with the driver and not Bolt and should be theoretical as you always have to book a ride through the applicable app. However, *Bolt could consider, to mitigate any such potential risk also in Norway by providing clear information to customers in the car that Bolt does not own the car and that the sticker is an ad or sign that the driver is registered on the Bolt app*.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], 

Please see below the assessment for *Finland*. 

We have not identified any specific requirements with regard to using campaigns and advertisements in the form of car-branding in the ride-hailing vertical. The following should however be taken into account when using branding on the cars:

* *Placement on the vehicle*: in principle, stickers must not be placed on the windshield or the front side windows (i.e. the stickers may not hinder the driver’s view) and reflective stickers may not be used either on the windshields or the front windows or elsewhere on the vehicle.
* *General rules regarding marketing*: the branding must comply with the general rules regarding marketing, i.e. it may not be inappropriate or against good practice, it cannot contain false or misleading information and it must clearly show its commercial purpose and on whose behalf marketing is carried out. Pursuant to Finnish case law, a company is free to refer to different types of cooperations with other companies. However, this must not be done in such a way as to mislead consumers as to the nature, scope, or relevance of the collaboration in the context at hand. Bearing in mind the set-up of the Bolt ride-hailing vertical, the driver being connected to the Bolt app in accordance with the terms and conditions set out between the driver and Bolt, *we do not believe such stickers indicating the cooperation between the driver and Bolt would result in any marketing issues such as misleading advertising*.
* *Reclassification risk*: The Finnish employment assessment is similar to the Swedish employment assessment. It can be noted that the distinction between employees, on the one hand, and independent contractors (i.e. consultants, self-employed etc.), on the other hand, is usually determined based on an overall assessment of all circumstances in each individual case. It seems unlikely that the Bolt sticker would – solely on its own – be decisive when determining whether the individual should be classified as an employee or not. However, we recommend adding e.g. the following text to the stickers to mitigate the risk “*Bolt is only an intermediary and the sticker is just a sign that the driver is registered on Bolt app*” or if it is not possible to include additional text to the stickers, then we recommend adding *a separate sticker* e.g. inside the vehicle which states that the driver is registered to the Bolt app.

Based on this final assessment, the recommendation for the Nordic market is essentially the same. There is no strict requirement or any specific wordings that need to be included but the recommendation is to include clarifying wording if possible. *There is no limitation regarding branding or advertising or the set-up that was proposed by tax*. The tax implications are essentially to be assessed by tax and not legal and I have therefore not looked into this any further.

Hi [~accountid:5da9b5832016b10c337ae434]! 

Below you can find answers to your request.

*Is the data filmed by the Driver considered personal data?*

The data recorded by the Driver on his TikTok account (name, pickup address, and a chat history with the Rider*) is considered personal data. This is because it leads to the identification of the Rider,* especially if the information is made public on social media platforms like TikTok, where the risk of identification by other users is significantly higher. There may be rare cases where this data would not be considered personal, but that does not apply to this situation.

*Did the Driver violate our rules by recording this data? If that’s the case, which rule?*

Since the recorded data is considered personal data, the *Driver has breached* [*clause 6 of the Privacy Notice for Drivers*|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/legal/ua/privacy-for-drivers/]*,* which states that Drivers _“_*_may not process the personal data of passengers_* _without the permission of us. You may not contact any passenger or collect, record, store, grant access, use or cross-use the personal data provided by the passenger or_ *_accessible to you via the Bolt app for any reason other than for the purposes of fulfilling the transportation services.”_* The concept of “_processing the data”_ also includes disclosing the data to anyone who, in particular, is not authorized to access this data (such as users of social media platform “TikTok”).

[Clause 6 of the Privacy Notice for Drivers|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/legal/ua/privacy-for-drivers/] also states that *if the Driver* *_“violates the requirements for the processing of personal data of passengers,_* _we (_*_Bolt) may terminate your drivers account and claim damages from you._*_”_

*What are our next steps?*

# We should *ask the Driver to immediately delete this video from TikTok and any other social media platforms where this video may have been posted.* Please provide a deadline for the removal and attach our explanation that the Driver has violated  our rules and the data is considered personal data.
# [According to Clause 6 of the Privacy Notice for Drivers|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/legal/ua/privacy-for-drivers/], *we may, at our sole discretion, delete his account and claim damages from him.* I cannot approve any termination of Driver's account in such a case. However, I think that it can be *approved by the CS Team.* I would recommend considering the termination of account *ONLY* in case the Driver fails to delete the video from TikTok and other social media platforms *OR* if this is not the first incident involving the same Driver.
# Please *check whether the Rider requested any compensation in any form*: promo code, material compensation, or other. If that's the case, we can also seek reimbursement for these expenses from the Driver. I also believe that t*he CS Team is an approver for this.*
# We reached out to our PR team for Ukraine in relation to this case. *The status of the final decision is to be announced (TBA) soon.*

So what happened here - 


If it’s a green dot and success and the amount is positive - it means the amount was charged from BB, which means Balance goes negative. If the Balance amount has *-* in front of the amount, it means it was paid back to BB, covering the debt. With rentals it depends, but often we charge the card with the pre-auth amount so as you can see from the Transaction history, the amounts charged to the card are usually small.

So starting with the first order from 23/05: 
*51.56 RON* charged from BB
Next one *81.02 RON* charged from BB
Then *59.85 RON*
And next one *50.68 RON*

51.56+81.02+59.85+50.68 = 243.11, so the customer’s Bolt Balance by that point becomes *-243.11 RON*



Onwards we can see in Transaction history that the BB amounts are negative, which means user is paying back to BB.

On 23/05/2023, 23:10, *-30.98 RON* to BB
Then *-50.68 RON*
And lastly *-59.85 RON* to BB.
Altogether 30.98+50.68+59.85= 141.51 RON

To sum it up, *243.11 RON - 141.51 RON = 101.6 RON*


The user then topped up their BB, because they probably saw that their Balance was negative by 101.60 and the top up covered their debt.

Hope this makes sense. If you have any questions, please let me know.

*Issue of nonactive cells in dynamic pricing cron*

It seems that backend does not store predictions if there is no surge for a specific cell. We need to update the code to explicitly send multiplier 1.0 in case of no surge.

Also, if the cell is not active, that cell is not even used for making predictions in a cron. This might impact calculation of the feature value. Let's assume we want to calculate average surge for the following two cells in 10-min window

* cell X: 10 model predictions in total, 9 model predictions returns no surge (multiplier=1), 1 model prediction returns multiplier=1.2 (cell was active from the beginning of the window)
* cell Y: inactive for first 9 prediction rounds (=no model predictions for this cell), active for the last prediction round in the last minute of the window (and model returns multiplier=1.2)

Because no data would be streamed for cell Y in the first 9 prediction rounds, avg_surge for cell Y for the full window would be 1.2, where the correct value would be 1.02. Solution to this issue is needed.

There are two models of collecting Spark metrics by Prometheus:

* pull-based model (default model in Prometheus): Promethus will periodically call Spark endpoint to collect metrics
* push-based model: Spark will send metrics to Prometheus Pushgateway, Prometheus will call Pushgateway periodically to collect metrics.



How to collect metrics in pull-based model:

* how to enable Spark metrics in Prometheus format: [https://stackoverflow.com/a/69874513|https://stackoverflow.com/a/69874513|smart-link] [https://dzlab.github.io/bigdata/2020/07/03/spark3-monitoring-1/|https://dzlab.github.io/bigdata/2020/07/03/spark3-monitoring-1/|smart-link] 
* Promethus needs to be able to connect to Spark endpoint. This might be an issue if Databricks is involved. An example notebook that uses a proxy to do this: [https://databrickslabs.github.io/overwatch/assets/_index/realtime_helpers.html|https://databrickslabs.github.io/overwatch/assets/_index/realtime_helpers.html|smart-link] 
* to enable some additional custom metrics at default Spark metrics paths, a generic Java class needs to created and provided as a jar file when initializing Spark. This has been tested and it works.

How to collect metrics in push-based model:

* Pushgateway needs to be set up
* Spark metrics in Prometheus format needs to be enabled 
* An example how to read Spark metrics at runtime and send it to Pushgateway in Pyspark: [https://gist.github.com/Lowess/3a71792d2d09e38bf8f524644bbf8349|https://gist.github.com/Lowess/3a71792d2d09e38bf8f524644bbf8349|smart-link]

{color:#bf2600}Email originally sent to CWA:{color}

Nous avons reçu un *courrier de l’URSSAF (en PJ)* concernant la situation de *travail dissimulé* signalée *à l’encontre de l’entreprise SAS SAFE DRIVER CAR.*

 

L’entreprise gère une flotte de véhicules et a recours aux services de centrale de réservation proposés par Bolt Operations OU. 

Comme vous pouvez le constater, l’URSSAF part du principe que Bolt, en sa *qualité de donneur d’ordre*, confie des prestations à l’entreprise qui est accusée de travail dissimulé et nous demande (i) d’enjoindre immédiatement l’entreprise de cesser l'exercice du travail dissimulé et (ii) de faire parvenir par retour de courrier certains documents. Elle nous conseille également de bloquer les sommes dues à la flotte jusqu’à nouvel ordre de l’URSSAF-même. 

Nous vous contactons car il s’agit du premier courrier de ce type et nous souhaiterions avoir votre aide pour rédiger une réponse. En effet, malgré notre volonté de collaborer avec les autorités, *nous considérons que l’URSSAF fait erreur quant à la relation contractuelle entre Bolt et le gestionnaire de flotte, d’où notre difficulté à donner suite à ses demandes.* 

Le gestionnaire de flotte (tout comme les chauffeurs indépendants ne travaillant pas sous une flotte), n’agit pas en tant que sous-traitant de Bolt. Bolt n’est qu’une centrale de réservation par le biais de laquelle les gestionnaires de flottes et les chauffeurs (à leur service ou indépendants) peuvent organiser la prise en charge des courses dans le cadre des prestations de services de transport effectuées pour et sur la base des indications du passager. 

Les gestionnaires de flottes s’adressent à Bolt lorsqu’ils souhaitent être mis en relation avec des passagers pour la réalisation de déplacements par leur intermédiaire. 

Conformément à ses obligations découlant du statut de centrale de réservation, Bolt vérifie au préalable des prestations de mise en relations (principalement lors de l'inscription des gestionnaires et des chauffeurs sur notre plateforme), certains documents tels que le permis de conduire et la carte professionnelle VTC.

Par ailleurs, Bolt n'est qu'une partie tierce à la relation contractuelle entre le gestionnaire de flotte et les chauffeurs VTC travaillant au sein de la flotte, les Conditions Générales Bolt pour les services de centrale de réservation étant souscrites par le gestionnaire de flotte.

Hi Paula, thanks for following up!

The issue is the following:

If a rider accepts a partial refund but wants it refunded to their payment method, in the UK agents always have to issue a full refund, even if the overcharge is, for example, 2 GBP in a 50 GBP trip.

Agents may check if the rider had previous orders that are close in price to the sum that needs to be refunded. Then they may process the full refund there, to avoid refunding the whole original order that is a lot more expensive. 

At this point this issue has been noticed and addressed only with one agent, however as Commerce team has confirmed such refunds may have serious implications for Bolt, I wanted to suggest adding this as a bullet point in the FAQ, to make sure there is absolute clarity.

I hope this clarifies, however please let me know!

What kind of gear would you like to start giving to couriers?
Independent contractor shall use their own equipment/tools for the provision of services, if the gear is provided by Bolt, it increases the reclassification risk.
However, in the Baltics reclassification risk is comparatively low (the lowest in LT, the risk may gradually increase upon adoption of the Platform Work directive). Moreover, we are already providing couriers with branded thermo-bags. Thus, an additional option to use, for example, branded jackets, should not substantially increase the existing risk. Thus, by analogy with the thermo-bag:

* use of additional gears should be optional
* Bolt should charge the deposit from the courier’s earnings for the use of the gear
* If the gear is not returned duly or not in good order upon the termination of the courier's account, Bolt may keep the deposit charged from the courier.

{{map_keys}} is a function for [MAP types|https://prestodb.io/docs/current/functions/map.html#map-functions] and does not work with [JSON types|https://prestodb.io/docs/current/functions/json.html#json-functions]. Unfortunately there doesn’t seem to be a {{keys()}} function for JSON available, but you can cast the JSON data to MAP first to make it work:

{code:sql}SELECT
  map_keys(data_as_map) AS keys,
  data
FROM (
  SELECT
    CAST(json_parse(data) AS MAP(VARCHAR, JSON)) AS data_as_map,
    data
  FROM ng_public.conditional_campaigns_bonus_calculation_log
)
LIMIT 10;{code}

Hello [~accountid:5f770d6325fbdf0068460e42] ,

It’s hard to predict query performance as it is highly dependent on data and its distribution/selectivity. 

The queries essentially insert based on:

{noformat}SELECT ${data.user_id}, ${data.type}, ${data.address}, ${data.lat}, ${data.lng}, ${data.place_id}, ${data.location_type}
WHERE
   (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ${TableNames.userFavoriteAddress} WHERE user_id = ${data.user_id} AND type = ${data.type}) = 0
{noformat}

{noformat}SELECT ${data.user_id}, ${data.type}, ${data.address}, ${data.lat}, ${data.lng}, ${data.place_id}, ${data.location_type}, ${data.name}, ${data.icon}
WHERE
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ${TableNames.userFavoriteAddress} WHERE user_id = ${data.user_id} AND type = ${data.type}) < ${maxLimit}{noformat}

These queries don’t make much sense to me and look malformed:

*  There is no FROM clause in outer SELECT, where is it getting the rows to send to INSERT?
* WHERE clause is strange. COUNT(*) will return a INT that is compared against 0 or {{< ${maxLimit}}}, returning true or false. If false it will fail and INSERT nothing. If true, it will insert all rows from table (the one should be in front of missing FROM). 


Unfortunately I can not give much advice based on the information provided. 
Note that query performance heavily relies on data, data distribution and SQL query itself, so it’s hard to predict without data samples to work with. Setting up local test environment with test data is the best way to obtain an idea about performance.

Hi Team,

The is a concern that the availability filter (AV) which is currently used in EE instead of the acceptance rate blocking (ARB) does not bring desired results and the cancellation rate is still high.  

[~accountid:712020:c0cc6249-3a02-4388-bba0-7e8370980ebe] for the context: AV was introduced because it is less driver’s freedom restrictive than ARB, therefore, less risky from a reclassification perspective.

* ARB – the driver is blocked from the platform if the ride acceptance rate drops below a certain level.
* AV has two types, we are currently testing No 2 in EE:

# Option No 1 “filtering” - after we have selected a list of drivers for matching with the order, we filter out, that is, decrease the number of drivers in the matching list, based on the model results. This can create situations, when there is a limited number of drivers and the order doesn’t match with any driver.
# Option No 2 "reordering" - we don’t decrease the list of drivers and instead assign priority weights in the queue, based on model results.

Per discussion with [~accountid:5ac755ce0a948a414408900a] the business is brainstorming the following new idea: moving drives from standard to basic category depending on the ride acceptance rate.  

* if the acceptance rate drops below a certain level, the driver who is providing services in the standard category will be moved to the basic category. Since the standard category has a higher price and we might provide rider discounts to encourage riders to use it or lower the commission, drivers should have the incentive to keep a high acceptance rate and stay in the standard category
*  poor quality cars that are in the basic category will not be able to get into the standard category even if the acceptance rate is high. It might, nevertheless, be an incentive to change the car. 
* In addition, the team is considering removing the opt-in option into a basic category, that is, good quality cars will stay in the standard category unless the acceptance rate drops below a certain level.

Hey [~accountid:628dd7111a437e0070426cb2] ! Since you’re taking this initiative, I wanted to share what I agreed on with Asia yesterday about managing incoming SD work for Rides 🙂 As of June, I’ll have the following approach:

* I’ve reserved 1 h every day to review newly assigned SD tickets
* Once it’s clear on an SD ticket what the issue, desired solution/outcome, and the required process change is, I’ll create a Jira task:
** If I have any capacity in the running sprint, I can add it to the sprint and action it
** If I don’t, I add it to the backlog
* If it was added to the backlog, I’d inform the ticket requester that I don’t have the capacity in the running month, and we’ll consider the required change when reviewing the plans for the next sprint at the end of the month
* At the end of the month, Asia and I will review what’s in the backlog to determine what I’ll pick up in the next sprint

For example, in June, my capacity is already maxed out, and I can’t take new work coming in from SD, so I’ll add the tasks to the Jira backlog. 

This is one way how to make the unplanned SD work a planned one 🙂 Hope this is useful for your project!

Hi [~accountid:610be972a539cb0068adf129] Please find below legal advice from our external counsel regarding discounts:

+*What can be discounted e.g., can we apply a blanket discount on the whole menu?*+ 

Under Maltese Law, Price Reductions are dealt with through the Price Indication Regulations (S.L 378.9). The Maltese transposition of the Price Indication Directive 2019/2161. S.L 378.9 does not refer to products that can or cannot be discounted. However, any announcement of a price reduction shall indicate the *prior price* applied by the trader for a determined period prior to the application of the price reduction. In this case, prior price means the lowest price applied by the trader for a determined period prior to the application of the price reduction.  

# In the case of goods which are liable to deteriorate or expire rapidly, the prior price refers to the price immediately before the price reduction;
# In the case of goods have been on the market for less than thirty (30) days, the prior price means the lowest price applied by the trader during this period;
# When the price reduction is progressively increased, the prior price is the price without the price reduction before the first application of the price reduction.

This means that whilst a blanket discount is possible, each product must still indicate its previous price, with certain exceptions for the three above-mentioned scenarios. Thus, it is highly recommended to confirm which products will be subject to such blanket discounts to ensure their proper reduction and subsequent identification.

+*How much can we discount e.g., are there any restrictions with regard to selling under the purchase price?*+ 

Under S.L 378.9, there are no other restrictions in this regard as long as the requirements identified in the previous query are satisfied.

+*How can we display discounts and are there any exceptions with regard to high-risk items such as alcohol/tobacco or other category?*+ 

Discounts have to be displayed in the manner identified in the first question above. 

S.L 378.9 does not refer to products such as alcohol/tobacco or any other category that is deemed ‘high-risk’. 

There are restrictions concerning alcohol but these are found in rules relating to *teleshopping* S.L. 350.24 - _"Cut-price Offers: Reference to "cut-price drinks", "happy hour drinks", "buy two and get one free", "money-off coupons" and similar advertisements or teleshopping that encourage excessive or immoderate consumption are unacceptable. Alcoholic drink retailers may however refer to price reductions for their stock."_

With reference to tobacco - advertising is prohibited in general.

+*Any other requirements to be aware of?*+ 

As per Rule 6 of S.L 378.9, the Provisions related to price +*indications*+ shall not apply to:  

(a) goods supplied for the purpose of re-selling. 

(b) goods sold in the course of the provision of a service. 

(c) sales by auction or sales of works of art or antiques. 

(d) an advertisement for such goods unless the selling price is indicated in the advertisement. 

Moreover, it would be prudent to keep in mind that as per Rule 10 of S.L 378.09, every trader shall take all necessary steps to ensure full compliance with these regulations; and even where any contravention of or non-compliance with any regulation may be attributed to any person in the employment of such trader, or in the exercise of any act or function authorized or permitted by the trader, proceedings shall also be taken against such trader.  

+*What penalties are there for non-compliance?*+ 

Offences against these regulations are dealt with through Rule 9 of S.L 378.9. 

Any person who contravenes any of these regulations shall, on conviction, be liable: 

(a) in the case of a first conviction, to a fine of not less than one hundred and fifty euro (€150) and not exceeding one thousand and five hundred euro (€1,500). 

(b) in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, to a fine of not less than two hundred euro (€200) and not exceeding two thousand euro (€2,000). 

The Courts may also, upon conviction, order the publication in one or more daily newspapers of the judgment, or a statement or summary thereof, passed on the offender. The Director General may also publish on the Malta Competition and Consumer Affairs Authority’s (MCCAA) website the judgment delivered by the Court, or a statement or summary thereof, passed on the offender.

*Query to lookup potentially missing active linking + active group membership payment method entries:*

_Returns_ *_zero hits_* _on prelive, let’s see what next week gives us._

{noformat}SELECT
	gm.business_user_group_id AS business_user_group_id,
	bu.business_company_id AS business_company_id,
    bugul.id AS business_user_global_user_linking_id
FROM business_user_global_user_linking AS bugul
JOIN business_user bu ON bu.global_user_linking_id = bugul.id
JOIN business_user_group_membership gm ON gm.business_user_id = bu.id
LEFT JOIN business_user_global_user_payment_method AS payment
  ON (payment.business_user_global_user_linking_id = bugul.id AND payment.business_company_id = bu.business_company_id AND payment.business_user_group_id = gm.business_user_group_id)
WHERE bugul.global_user_id IS NOT NULL AND payment.id IS NULL AND gm.state = "active";{noformat}

{quote}That’s correct, we want to insert nothing if the predicate is false.{quote}

If you know ahead of time that this holds up, there is no point in counting the number of rows. Simply {{INSERT INTO.. . SELECT FROM}} and if there are zero rows, nothing will be inserted. Counting is extra work that brings no benefit.

{quote}I thought that’s where I would need your input. I can have some feeling about whether the queries are performing better or worse, but will it translate well to our mysql hosts?{quote}

The query optimiser makes decisions based on data it has. Without data it’s not possible to get accurate picture of how query will behave, even for  DBAs. 😉
A query might run fine on a small table (doing full table scan) but will not scale on large table and will need indexing. What DBAs do is run EXPLAIN to see how the query optimiser behaves and then try to do query tuning. My advice is:


#  Use local env to create table and generate random data to populate it.
# Pick queries to examine, make sure they are syntactically valid, then run EXPLAIN against the query.
# Examine EXPLAIN plans
# For assistance with step 3, share with DBAs: table definition, valid queries (we prefer SQL to NodeJS code) and EXPLAIN output
# …
# Profit 🙂

Hey [~accountid:610d04058c15ca006f9988a6] there are two ways how to arrange a commission increase:

# Friendly, legally compliant, but time-consuming
## If the commission is separately agreed with every restaurant in special terms, the legally correct way is to prepare an amendment in writing.
## Preparing an amendment and arranging signing requires an individual approach to every partner - this is a time-consuming and burdensome task for the local team.
# Business aggressive, but effective
## Sending email notifications to all the partners about the commission increase without asking them to sign the amendment. If the partner disagrees, it shall send Bolt a termination notice, the cooperation will be terminated after 30 days of the receipt of the termination notice. 
## The email notification is quite an aggressive and business-unfriendly approach, but it is tolerated by the legal team globally to reduce the workload of signing amendments.
## Please note that the special terms state that: “T_he Special Terms of the Agreement may be amended by the parties’ agreement in a form reproducible in writing”_. Since there will be no agreement in writing, partners can dispute the validity of such changes. Thus, if you try out this approach, but some partners disagree, we rather sign the proper amendment with them.

It is for the business to decide which approaches to choose, assessing the pros and cons of both.

At the time of my previous comment, this password could be only created by Bolt employees, and never changed.

Once credentials are lost, another account was created instead, and lost one got removed, by Bolt employees.

Password is autogenerated, 8 chars long. This policy was chosen (I assume) to keep password short and simple for app workers to not to loose access to the app. Also, these credentials is not possible to use from multiple devices. Once logged in from new device, previous sessions expire in matter of minutes. This event, in case of illegal activities, would cause “getting offline” experience for real users, and result in them contacting our Support team.

Keeping all of that in mind, it *was* acceptable for us to keep password policy unchanged.

*But,* since then, we have implemented credentials restore mechanisms (with additional logic to password policy, I have to check), plus, keeping audit’s interest to the reported issue in mind, I feel that we need to re-raise this topic, and look into ways of improving it.

Hi Rijntje, 

Super super leuk je net gesproken te hebben. :) Aan creatieve ideeën en mogelijkheden zal het zeker niet liggen!! 

Even kort de vier ideeën die nu op tafel liggen. Voor nu goed als we alles even laten bezinken en ook intern bespreken wat er mogelijk is. Zoals je zei zijn jullie een erg data-driven bedrijf, dus goed om te weten wat er ook technisch gezien mogelijk is (in de app/aanleveren website content etc.). 

Hieronder de vier besproken ideeën:

# *Digitale tips in de app & de limited edition fysieke versies.* We leveren een jaar lang tips aan, gelinkt aan het seizoen en bijvoorbeeld feestdagen. Zo krijgen mensen tijdens hun rit iets te doen, er kan bijvoorbeeld een pop-up komen +in de app+. In de winter kan dit zijn: _Zit je lekker warm in de Bolt en verveel je je tijdens je rit? Check dan hier de door Barts Boekje geselecteerde lekkerste kaasfondue restaurants._ Of in de zomer: _dit zijn de leukste picknick plekken waar we je naartoe kunnen brengen bij je volgende rit._ We maken van te voren een planning welke thema's we pakken, en leveren jullie hier tips voor aan. Ook bespraken we het idee van de +limited edition fysieke boekjes+. Deze kunnen we later uitrollen nadat we in de app hebben getest hoe er gereageerd wordt op de tips. Het lijkt me interessant om er een collectie/collectors item van te maken (bijvoorbeeld een reeks van 4), zodat je al deze boekjes wilt sparen, Bolt gebruikers aanspoort om een bepaalde actie te doen, en hier dan een beloning aan te koppelen zoals een maand lang gratis Bolt ritten. Zo spoor je mensen aan om bij hun volgende rit toch voor Bolt te kiezen (i.p.v. Uber), want ze willen deze collectors items sparen. Daarnaast willen ze natuurlijk de exclusieve tips ontvangen in de app. Je kunt dit zien als PR campagne, maar mij lijkt het juist te gek om dit een standaard van Bolt te maken. Mensen gaan wellicht op een gegeven moment veel waarde aan deze 'extra' hechten, en zo kunnen we er continuïteit in houden. 
# *Umbrella Game* - zie bijlage
# *We leveren content aan voor routes die jullie door Amsterdam willen gaan maken.* Dit zijn geen de toeristische routes waar je langs het Rijksmuseum of het Leidseplein gaat, maar je gaat bijvoorbeeld vintage shoppen in dat kleine straatje X, of je gaat lunchen bij de nieuwe trattoria die nog niet veel mensen kennen. Wij stellen deze routes samen. Zoals ik vertelde is één van mijn collega's de oprichtster van de stadswandeling, dus kan ik met het volste vertrouwen zeggen dat we de kneepjes van het vak héél goed kennen. :)
# *We leveren website content aan met tips die Bolt mag gebruiken*

Ik ben even kwijt of de *Local Heroes* bij punt 3 of punt 4 past haha. Stuur jij mij hier nog een briefing voor. Dan kijk ik even hoe wij hierop in kunnen haken. 

Oké veel food for thought, waar we gelukkig het hele weekend (in het zonnetje met een lekker drankje op het strand ;;)) over na kunnen denken! 

Ik ben ontzettend benieuwd naar wat jij verder nog op papier gaat zetten, en hoe deze plannen zich vorm gaan geven. Als dat wat concreter is, kunnen we gaan kijken welke prijskaartjes erbij komen. 

Echt te gek, ik krijg in ieder geval enorm veel energie van onze plannen.

Hi Rijntje, 

Super super nice to have just spoken to you. :) There will definitely be no shortage of creative ideas and possibilities!!! 

Just a quick note of the four ideas that are currently on the table. For now, it's good if we let everything sink in and also discuss the possibilities internally. As you said, you are a very data-driven company, so good to know what is also technically possible (in the app/supply website content etc.). 

Here are the four ideas discussed:
Digital tips in the app & the limited edition physical versions. We deliver one-year tips linked to the season and holidays, for example. This will give people something to do during their ride, for example, there could be a pop-up in the app. In winter, this could be: Are you sitting nice and warm in the Bolt and bored during your ride? Then check out the tastiest cheese fondue restaurants selected by Barts Boekje here. Or in summer: these are the nicest picnic spots we can take you to on your next ride. We plan in advance which themes we'll tackle, and provide you with tips for this. We also discussed the idea of limited edition physical booklets. We can roll these out later after testing in the app how the tips are responded to. I think it would be interesting to make it a collection/collectors item (e.g. a series of 4), so that you want to save all these booklets, encourage Bolt users to do a certain action, and then attach a reward to this such as a month of free Bolt rides. That way you encourage people to choose Bolt (instead of Uber) on their next ride anyway, because they want to save these collectors' items. In addition, of course, they want to receive the exclusive tips in the app. You can see this as a PR campaign, but to me it seems just too crazy to make this a standard of Bolt. People might start to value this 'extra' a lot at some point, and this way we can keep continuity in it.
Umbrella Game - see attachment
We provide content for routes that you want to create through Amsterdam. These are not the tourist routes where you go past the Rijksmuseum or Leidseplein, but you go vintage shopping in that little street X, for example, or you have lunch at the new trattoria that not many people know about yet. We put together these itineraries. As I told you, one of my colleagues is the founder of the city walk, so I can say with full confidence that we know the ropes lol. :)
We provide website content with tips that Bolt may use
I am momentarily lost as to whether Local Heroes fits under point 3 or point 4 haha. You send me a briefing on this. Then I'll take a look at how we can tie in with this. 

Okay, lots of food for thought, which we can happily spend the whole weekend thinking about (in the sun with a nice drink on the beach ;;))! 

I am very curious to know what else you will put on paper, and how these plans will unfold.

Frontend engineers discussed this issue several times already without any new conclusions apart from the fact that it was a known issue in the Beehive some time ago to improperly manage migrations between local storage schemas and not clear old contents of the local storage.

If the UI part responsible for managing those areas of the local storage were removed, agents remained with dangling entries which sometimes influenced how backend queries were formed.

This particular issue has been fixed, after which we haven’t heard of similar reports.

As for the issue with the 2 agents in the report, several of the self-troubleshooting points should have helped triaging the issue:

* clearing local storage
* checking in a different browser

We can relate this to an increased volume of irregular requests in recent weeks. Bolt is currently getting targeted by some fraud through SMS pumping (requests).

Sadly we cannot directly restrict the user number as this would require a significant amount of resources and work through hardcoding. However, these attacks are being mitigated by our rules and restrictions anyways, meaning that if a phone number is related to such an attack, our engine will start restricting these requests and the user should be “saved” from the alerts.

We have suspended any devices in relation to these requests but it is definitely not a permanent solution due to the fraudsters being dynamic and switching things up. You may advise the customer not to respond to any of these requests and to be ensured that as long as they do not share their code, their account is safe. And to further clarify then if the number owner does not have an account with us then one will NOT be created unless the verification with a code is completed.

All the best,
Mattias

Hi Vasilina,

Apologies for the late reply.

This is the error coming from the payment provider side, which is very serious as it means that the payment method provider suspects fraud. Usually, it takes a day for the payment provider to do their own check, determine that the user is not a fraudster, and let the user continue using the payment method. We have the option to whitelist the user. It is risky since it means giving the green light for all time to the specific payment method and the user, even if they are in fraudsters' hands. However, you are always welcome to report these kinds of cases to us, and if we consider that there is very little chance of the user becoming a fraudster in the future, we will whitelist the card.

Best,

Leyla

Hi team, 

we are re-opening the ticket due to the ongoing discussions on branding. 

As a general comment: branding set up for FR has been assessed and designed along with OC to mitigate the reclassification risks related to the branding. In fact the sticker might be misunderstood as being a uniform giving the wrong impression that driver belongs to Bolt personnel, the car belongs to Bolt, the driver takes rides exclusively with via Bolt...  Therefore it is utmost important  to consider and display any sums paid pursuant to branding program in FR as advertising services. 

We thought it would be useful to address some concerns around signing and tax and make sure we are all on the same page. 

*A. Signing*

* As previously discussed, +the ideal solution+ for FR would be to have the branding advertisement agreement signed ( “_acceptation expresse_”) by the independent  driver/fleet owner whereby  drivers/fleets agree to provide advertising services in exchange for a specific remuneration, which means that we could better defend ourselves if in the event branding is leveraged by the driver in the framework of a reclassification lawsuit. 
* However, if Spotdraft signature is causing issues and complexity to reach your goals, we can discuss an +alternative solution+ that consists in: 

1/ *email sent* to the independent driver/fleet owner *with the branding terms*  (both General and Specific Terms) *attached as a PDF prior* (or on the day at the latest) *to the day the sticker is being installed.* 



2/ *tracking the effective date* ( ie the day the sticker is installed) along with the third-party provider applying the stickers.



3/ making sure the driver sends evidence of the *sticker being still on the car at the end of the first  month* as of application and showing his tacit acceptance of terms (signature of the contract  by means of *“**_acceptation tacite_*_”_) 

*Nota Bene:* Risk is high but limited to the first month; indeed as the contract is communicated by email to the driver just at the time of his subscription to the program. If the sticker is still on the car after 1 month in accordance with the contract, he will be deemed to have ratified the contract by his behaviour.





*B. Tax considerations*

 [~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c] : in case you are not aware under the recommended contractual set up rolled out couple of months ago, branding is considered as a standalone advertising service provided by driver/fleet to Bolt and remunerated as follows: 

* *flat monthly fee : 100€*

*NB* : it s important to have a +*fixed remuration*+ for this service. Indeed in the past only  “retrocommissions” (cashback) were paid and even though t_he program w_as not mandatory, Bolt was incentivising financially the drivers to opt for it and thus indirectly to work mainly for its platform and put them in a position of dependency, which could have been considered by judges as a clue characterizing an employment relationship between the driver and Bolt;

* + in same cases ( [~accountid:61e918be38041c00686ad2bf] to confirm)*a variable fee KPIs-related ( 8% “retrocommission” / cash back )  based on rides.*

Under this set up whereby driver/fleet acts as a advertising service provider,  we understand that:

* the driver  should provide an invoice to Bolt (in accordance with section 5.2 Branding General terms “_Where You are required to do so by law, You will provide Bolt with a valid VAT invoice for all charges paid to You under this Agreement, in accordance with Your legal obligations.”);_ 
*  the *fee paid by Bolt to the driver/fleet owner for advertising services should not be treated as KPI-related transportation service fees/ bonuses.* 

→ Can someone let us know *if and how such remuneration appears on the weekly reports* shared with driver (“_relevés des sommes versées_”) ? 

Team, feel free to organise a meeting if you want to discuss the above further. 

Thanks,

Michela and Emilie

*_Summary:_* 

* The right to sell medicinal products at a distance is granted to a specific general pharmacy which has applied for the right of distance selling. Activities related to the distance sale of medicinal products can only take place at the place of business.
* The exception for which the right to handle medicinal products is not required is for the services used for the delivery of medicinal products, but it can only be made on the basis of risk analysis regarding the arrangement of the delivery of medicines and conditions affecting it prepared by the pharmacy authorisation holder.
* The authorisation holder must also carry out regular control over the delivery of medicinal products. Before closing the transport packaging, it must check the completeness of the packaging and document the performed control.

According to your description, you want to mediate the medicines of existing Internet pharmacies and provide a courier service. The intermediation of medicines from existing Internet pharmacies by someone else is not possible nor permitted. 

Provision of courier service to a pharmacy is permitted only under the above conditions. It is not permitted to reflect pharmacies' medicinal products range on the Bolt application. The sale of medicines elsewhere without authorization is a prohibited economic activity and is punishable.

{noformat}WITH conditional_campaigns as (
SELECT DISTINCT 
      pe.target_id
      , pe.campaign_id
      , car.normalized_reg_number
      , pe.id as period_enrollment_id      
      --, condition_id
      , JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(log.data, '$.company_id') as company_id
      /*  In Billing system we don't have granularity on conditions 
       * 	hence we can't add it here --> will cause duplicates   */
      --, JSON_EXTRACT(log.data, '$.number_of_branded_trips') as trips
      --, JSON_EXTRACT(log.data, '$.contributions') as driver_contributions
      --, JSON_EXTRACT(log.earned_bonuses, '$[0].bonus.amount') as bonus_1
      --, JSON_EXTRACT(log.earned_bonuses, '$[1].bonus.amount') as bonus_2
      --, JSON_EXTRACT(log.earned_bonuses, '$[2].bonus.amount') as bonus_3
      --, log.earned_bonuses
      --, log.last_ingested as calc_last_update
      --, log.created_date
FROM ng_public.conditional_campaigns_period_enrollment pe
LEFT JOIN ng_public.conditional_campaigns_bonus_calculation calc on calc.period_enrollment_id =pe.id
LEFT JOIN ng_public.conditional_campaigns_condition cond on cond.id = calc.condition_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public.conditional_campaigns_bonus_calculation_log log on log.id = calc.bonus_calculation_log_id 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.fleet_car car on car.id = pe.target_id
WHERE --pe.campaign_id IN (834,850)
--AND pe.target_id = 4838030
--AND 
pe.created_date > DATE('2023-05-14')
AND calc.created_date > DATE('2023-05-14')
AND log.created_date > DATE('2023-05-14')
),
billing_raw as (
select
rc.compensation_uid as uid,
rc.group_id as period_enrollment_id,
rc.to_agent_type as agent_type,
rc.to_agent_id as agent_id,
od.property_value as car_id,
min(date_trunc('day',DATE_ADD('hour', timezone_hour(at_timezone(r.handling_timestamp , asc2.timezone)), r.handling_timestamp))) as balance_exported_date,
sum(r.sum_with_vat) as sum_with_vat
from ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_record_compensation rc
left join ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_record r on r.id = rc.record_id 
left join (select organic_event_id, property_key, property_value from ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_organic_event_details where property_key = 'car_id' group by 1,2,3) od on od.organic_event_id = r.organic_event_id
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = r.city_id 
where rc.compensation_uid_type = 'branding_bonus'
and r.balance_state = 'exported'
group by 1,2,3,4,5
), 
billing_final as (
select 
period_enrollment_id,
agent_type,
agent_id,
balance_exported_date,
cast(car_id as integer) as car_id,
sum(sum_with_vat) as sum_with_vat
from billing_raw
group by 1,2,3,4,5
)
select 
cc.*,
bf.agent_type,
bf.agent_id,
bf.balance_exported_date,
bf.sum_with_vat
from conditional_campaigns cc 
left join billing_final bf on bf.period_enrollment_id = cc.period_enrollment_id and bf.car_id = cc.target_id {noformat}

{noformat}with lost_with_0 as 
(select 
	e.vehicle_id,
	e.created as lost_moment
from ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event e
left join ng_rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc ON e.search_category_id  =sc.id
left JOIN ng_rental.rental_fleet_vehicle v ON e.vehicle_id=v.id
left JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city c ON sc.city_id=c.id
where e.to_state = 'lost' and e.created_date >date'2023-06-01' and e.charge=0
)
select
	'heartbeat' as event_type,
    v.model AS model,
    c.id AS city_id,
    ce.vehicle_id,
    ce.created,
    JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(value_json, '$.location.charge') AS charge,
    lost_moment
FROM ng_rental.rental_order_vehicle_custom_event ce
left join ng_rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc ON cast(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(value_json, '$.state.search_category_id') as int)=sc.id
left JOIN ng_rental.rental_fleet_vehicle v ON ce.vehicle_id=v.id
join lost_with_0 l0 on ce.vehicle_id = l0.vehicle_id and ce.created between date_add('hour',-48,l0.lost_moment) and l0.lost_moment 
JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city c ON sc.city_id=c.id
WHERE event_type = 'location_heartbeat'
and ce.created_date>date'2023-06-01' and c.id=1
union all 
select 
	'ride' as event_type,
	    v.model AS model,
	city_id,
	o.vehicle_id,
	o.created,
	null as charge,
	lost_moment
FROM ng_rental.rental_order_order o 
left JOIN ng_rental.rental_fleet_vehicle v ON o.vehicle_id=v.id
join lost_with_0 l0 on o.vehicle_id = l0.vehicle_id and o.created between date_add('hour',-48,l0.lost_moment) and l0.lost_moment 
JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city c ON o.city_id=c.id
WHERE o.state = 'finished'
and o.created_date>date'2023-06-01' and c.id=1
order by vehicle_id asc, lost_moment asc, created asc{noformat}

I am checking the VAT treatment with Baker.  Since the vouchers will be used for ride hailing only, it is very likely that it will be treated as single purpose voucher instead of multiple purpose voucher (when VAT rate is unknown at the time of issuance).  The problem of single purpose voucher is, we need to pay VAT at the time we issue the vouchers not at the time it is spent.  When the vouchers are void or expired, then we can claim back the VAT.  Since we don’t have any tracking when the vouchers are expired (and I assume we would not want to invoice Worksmile when the vouchers are issued), it could risk VAT leakage.  Therefore, I am checking if there is any possibility we can treat the vouchers as multiple purpose voucher in this case with the argument that some drivers are VAT registered and some are not (and thus VAT rate is unknown at the time of issuance).

Will get back once we hear anything from Baker.

However, please note, that per the below reply (a similar question was asked already in March 2020) only pharmacists can dispense medicines from pharmacies. Thus, ordinary couriers cannot deliver medicine. Thus, either the courier shall have certain medical qualifications or the medicine although ordered online shall be picked up in the pharmacy (it beats the whole idea of delivery). Considering all the constraints, I advise considering other markets for testing medicine delivery.

“Täname initsiatiivi üles näitamast, kuid peame teie ettepanekule eitavalt vastama. Selgitame, et kirjeldatud tegevus vastab ravimite kaugmüügile ja ravimite kaugmüügi õigus on ainult üldapteegi tegevusloa omajal, kellele on see õigus antud (RavS § 31 lg 51-56 , § 38 lg 1 p 3) alusel. Praegu on Eestis kaks kaugmüügiõigusega ehk internetiapteeki. Teised üldapteegid võivad samast apteegist ostetud ravimeid kliendi soovil kohale toimetada. Ravimeid võib elanikele väljastada vaid apteegist, mistõttu ei saa ravimeid tellida eraisikult või -ettevõttelt. Ravimeid võivad apteegist väljastada vaid proviisor ja farmatseut. Ravimite väljastamisel on vajalik patsienti nõustada ravimi õigest ja ohutust kasutamisest. Ravimite tellimine telefoni või muul teel ei ole apteegist, sh internetiapteegist, lubatud. Seega  ei ole BOLT-il  võimalik oma platvormi kaudu ravimeid müüa ja neid isikutele kätte toimetada.

Samas ei ole välistatud posti- ja kullerteenuse kasutamine apteegi poolt ravimite kättetoimetamisel. Ravimite kohaletoimetamise eest vastutajaks (sh transpordikorraldus) on apteek. Apteek saab hinnata esmalt kullerteenusega seotud riske ja kui need on maandatud, siis apteegiteenuse osutaja saab sõlmida lepingu kullerteenuse osutajaga ravimite kättetoimetamiseks.

 Kokkuvõttes ei võimalda tänane seadusandlus ega ka eriolukord hälbimist tegevusloa nõuetest, kuid kullerteenuse osutamine eelpool mainitud tingimustel (apteek näeb vajadust, hindab riske ja sõlmib lepingu) on võimalik.

On selge, et eriolukord võib tekitada teistsuguseid lähenemisi, aga hetkel tuleb lähtuda kirjasolevast.“

*ENG translation* 

Thank you for taking the initiative, but we have to say no to your proposal. We would like to clarify that the activity described corresponds to the distance selling of medicinal products and that only the holder of a general pharmacy licence has the right to sell medicinal products at a distance, which is granted on the basis of § 31(51) to (56), § 38(1)(3) of the Pharmacy Act. Currently, there are two pharmacies in Estonia with a distance selling right, i.e. internet pharmacies. Other general pharmacies may deliver medicines purchased from the same pharmacy at the customer's request. Medicines can only be dispensed to residents by a pharmacy, which means that medicines cannot be ordered from a private individual or company. Only pharmacists and pharmacists can dispense medicines from pharmacies. When dispensing medicines, it is necessary to advise the patient on the correct and safe use of the medicine. It is not permitted to order medicines by telephone or other means from a pharmacy, including an internet pharmacy. Therefore, BOLT is not able to sell and deliver medicines to individuals through its platform.

However, the use of postal and courier services by the pharmacy for the delivery of medicines is not excluded. The pharmacy is responsible for the delivery of medicines (including transport arrangements). The pharmacy can first assess the risks associated with the courier service and, once these have been mitigated, the pharmacy service provider can contract with the courier service provider to deliver the medicines.

In conclusion, neither the current legislation nor the specific situation allows for derogation from the requirements of the licence, but the provision of courier services under the conditions mentioned above (pharmacy sees the need, assesses the risks and enters into a contract) is possible.

It is clear that an emergency situation may give rise to different approaches, but for the moment we must proceed on the basis of what is written”

Hi Sabina!

You’re saying “If we change it around and reply to the user first and then mark the case as {{pending}}, the user gets notified since we make a public reply, and they might reply, but if they do, the case re-opens, and the agent will have to deal with it again, which is the issue we are trying to avoid in point 1.” - if this happens the agent wouldn’t have to “deal” with the case again because it’s still solved in another ticket. If the customer asks new/additional questions then yes, we would need to work this case but if the user has new/additional questions they would probably reach out anyway. Also this wouldn’t impact the FRT because the first reply would already be there - which was the issue that we highlighted in the 1st point. 

Overall, I’m not really following what are we afraid of when it comes to changing this process? That in X amount of cases the user would still reply to the duplicate? We already have examples of this happening even if we don’t reply. Any other major risks that we see?

I strongly believe that in this case we don’t need to invest time into gathering data to prove that one way is better than the other and we should use common sense when we think about what is best for our users.

Also what type of impression it leaves of us as a company when we ignore some cases and never reply? Yes, internally we know that we did reply to the duplicate case but the user doesn’t have this confirmation. They might actually start thinking that they need to create several tickets each time to get our attention because not all cases get picked up by our CS.

_Further, while the amount of documentation might be considerable also within a market section, in our case one can disregard all documentation about Bolt’s rental products (Drive and Micromobility), but also all driver-facing ride-hailing documents._

# _Passenger T&C - global version_ [_here_|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-riders/]
# _Marketplace Conduct Guidelines for Riders - global version_ [_here_|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/]
# _Passenger privacy policy - global version_ [_here_|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/privacy-for-riders/]
# _Global Privacy Notice on Video Surveillance - global version_ [_here_|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance/]_._
