Hey [~accountid:61261fa2dd25520076a72c06], [~accountid:6345c2cd5efe6ce125d8176b], though as I am aware the legal research re the data extraction is currently on hold, we still got the memorandum from the external advisor in Azerbaijan that was requested before such decision to put the research on hold. Sharing the memorandum with you so you have more visibility on this topic.

The main points to note:

# +Contractual liability+: T&Cs of Uber and Yango *prohibit the extraction of data*, while T&Cs of Maxim do not contain such prohibition.
# +Protection of data set+: Information on ETA of the route and route fare would be classified as the data set. In case such data would be a result of creative input, *which is not very likely in this case*, such data extraction could be classified as a breach of copyright. 
However, such scraping of data could amount to *breach of special right of protection of data set.* This breach would arise in case where the activity results in *preventing the normal use of the website and slowing down the website* (or even temporary failure of website, for example) and any similar situations which causes harm the legitimate interests of the producer. In absence of this, any related risk  of liability would be insignificant (10-20%). 
# +Commercial secret+: If as a result of the information received from the site, not only the price and ETA, but a *formula, method in the competitor's commercial activity* is learned as a result of this information, this is a commercial secret and *a violation of the requirements of the law.* However, this should not be the case in our situation.
# +Unfair competition+: Data scraping activity could result in violation of the Law on Unfair Competition *in case it causes deliberate disruption, interruption and stopping the competitor's business relations by illegal means.* Such deliberate disrupting, interrupting and stopping of the competitor's business could include *blocking, stopping or slowing down the application and/or the site of the competitor*. At the same time, it should also not be applicable in our case. 
# +Scraping by an employee+: If data scraping has been performed by an employee due to performance of their job functions, the employer is automatically liable for such actions of their employee (no-fault liability).
# +Third-party service provider+: When a third-party service provider performs data sraping activities, Bolt is not liable provided that the third party has been acting independently. This means that where the third party is an independent entity which provides the similar services for other clients as well professionally, such relations will not be classified as dependent agent relations. However, where Bolt has a supervision over the third party, or if Bolt has obtained such services through third parties specifically to avoid its liability, Bolt would be held liable. 
# +Manual vs. automatic extraction:+ The laws do not define a difference for manual or automated methods for data extraction in terms of the legality of the action _per se._
# +Criminal liability+: Bolt would not be criminally liable for the actions of third party service provider. However, Bolt would be liable for the actions of its employee where it is proved that the illegal action of the employee is caused by the failure of Bolt to manage control over that employee. At the same time, if the data extraction activity does not cause *intentional damage, deletion, corruption, alteration or blocking of computer data* by a person who does not have the right to do so and causes significant damage, or *deliberately seriously hindering the operation of the computer system* by a person who does not have the right to do so by entering, transmitting, damaging, deleting, spoiling, changing or blocking computer data, *there is no risk* for criminal liability.

Please let me know if you have any questions re the above.

[^05.06_legal opinion_data extraction_Bolt services AZ.pdf]

Hey [~accountid:6012ba328fb6ea014a8294ce], below is the information provided by the external advisor re the procedure for obtaining an advertisement permit in Azerbaijan.

Please let me know if you need further support here.

----

Under Sub-Section 25.1 of Law No. 1281-IVQ, dated 15 May 2015, of the Republic of Azerbaijan, _On Advertisement,_(the “*Advertisement Law*”), an advertising in vehicles is placed either on the vehicle or in its interior based on a contract concluded between the owner of the vehicle and the advertising distributor or advertising agent.

Under Sub-Section 25.2 of the Advertisement Law, an approval from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan (the “*Ministry*”) is required for such advertising.

The advertisement contract is among the documents that must be submitted to the Ministry in order to receive the approval. Pursuant to Sub-Section 2.6.1 of the “Administrative regulation on acceptance of application and documents for granting approval to placing advertising on vehicles”, approved by Decision No. Q75-001-12, dated 30 November 2012, of the Collegium of the Ministry (the “*Regulations*”), the following documents must be submitted to the Ministry by the car owner along with the relevant application form:

·       a copy of the contract concluded between the advertiser and the owner of the vehicle,

·       a copy of the inspection act of the Ministry on the technical condition of the vehicle and the suitability of its external appearance for advertising placement,

·       layout of the advertising to be placed on a vehicle, and

·       details of vehicle(s) on which advertising will be placed (state registration number, registration certificate number and the date of issue).

Absent inconsistencies or grounds for rejection, the decision to grant the permit is communicated to the applicant by email in form of a notice about the date, time and place where the applicant can collect the “Passport on technical conditions for advertising placed on vehicles” (Regulations, Sub-Section 3.3.4).

Paragraph 3 of the Standards (defined below) specifically provides that permit to placing an advertisement on a vehicle is issued by the Ministry in the form of passport of technical terms of advertisement, and the advertisement is so placed subject to obtaining the passport.

*The process is performed free of charge.*

Consequently, *conclusion of advertising agreements with drivers (car owners) will not eliminate the requirement to procure the relevant approval from the Ministry by the relevant drivers (car owners).*

The Code of the Administrative Violations imposes a liability in the amount of AZN30 to AZN50 on individuals, AZN150 to AZN200 on officers, and AZN1,500 to AZN2,000 on entities for placing advertisement on a car without approval (or failing to comply with the rules of such advertisement).

Meanwhile, under Sub-Section 25.5 of the Advertisement Law, placing distinctive signs on a vehicle that indicate belonging to a certain person is not considered an advertising. For instance, if a vehicle is owned by Bolt, placing a “Bolt” logo on it will not be considered as advertising.

Further, *there are no separate requirements for advertising permits applicable for private cars and taxis. Distinctive badge is not listed among the documents that must be submitted along with an application for the permit.*

Hi Colleagues,

Confirmed with Baker, the vouchers can be treated as multiple purpose voucher and therefore no issue with the VAT.  The correct treatment should be like this:

If we assume:

*  Bolt issued 100 vouchers with $5 face value each on 7th June → No action required regarding VAT reporting upon the issuance
* A rider spend one voucher on 8th June (full ride price is $20 and he paid $15 and the voucher) → Driver should issue a fiscal receipt of $20 to rider (which ride fee is $18.5 + $1.5 VAT in the case that the driver is VAT registered)

Hi [~accountid:61124fbdec92ab0070270a33] 

I’ve reached out to the external counsel MRA to assess remedies and opportunity of appealing the Prefetto’s decision (against Bolt) in Turin. 

As discussed yesterday, we can appeal the decision before the *Giudice di Pace* (competent court for low value disputes). Since we don’t have the proof of receipt of the notification of the Prefetto deicision, the *deadline to appeal is 16/06* ( aka 30 days as of 17/05 - dated stamped on the notification).  

 *MRA is of the view that it is worth appealing if Bolt wants to build up a case-law to challenge future decisions of the competent authorities regarding similar cases.*



However please consider that: 

# Some *judges do not consider themselves to be competent to decide on the merits of the cas*e ( ie whether the fine is lawful or not), but only regarding procedural issues concerning the Prefect’s decision (_eg._ the decision was notified after the time limit).
# The Prefetto rarely participates in the proceedings held in court which means that there might not be a *contradictory phase* on this matter:
##  If the Prefect does not appear in the proceeding, Bolt will have the possibility to present their arguments without contradiction from another party. 
## Otherwise, if the Prefect appears in the proceeding, Bolt will have the opportunity to examine the documentation on which the Prefect based his decision, and therefore to contest such documentation and their decision.

Both options might be positive for us, though.

3. In the event of a favorable decision for Bolt, there *won’t be any automatic binding effect on the future cases* for other fines before the Giudice di Pace, specially in a different city and all pending applications with the Prefetto for the same lack of identification numbers are not cancelled. 



*SANCTION*

If the Court rules against Bolt, Bolt shall pay:

* the amount ordered by the Prefect (in this specific case, the injunction amounts to *€ 203,29*);
* potentially the reimbursement of the *counter party’s legal fees*. However, generally, in appeals against the Prefect decision, the Justice of the Peace opts for the application of the principle of compensation where each party pays their own fees.



*FEES if Bolt wants to appeal:*

Legal costs for the proceeding are: 

* *800EUR + expenses and VAT for MRA Legal assistance* 
* *43 EUR to be paid upfront* 



+Proposal of internal arrangements+ 

If you want to proceed, *Legal is willing to pay 800 EUR + miscellaneous* for the legal assistance as this is the first time that we deal with such a case and could be beneficial for future cases. We also believe that could be useful to understand the reasoning of the local authorities when it comes to bad parking. Furthermore, the document disclosure in Court could help understanding the Police procedures ( eg perhaps they did take pictures of the vehicle or they have additional documents to identify it even if they didn’t note the number on the report). 

Just to clarify the expectations, whilst we support you on this case, we cannot engage in legal/judiciairy fees for trial for any future fine. This would not sustainable and not worthy either. 

*43EUR to enrol the case in Court + eventually the accrued fine in case of negative outcome, would be on the Business.* Would this work for you?

Please let me know if you want to proceed and if you agree on the split of the fees. 

Grazie!

Michela

Hey team! As per last comment I have requested Fred’s opinion on this topic. As this conversation goes through two SD tickets and around 40 messages I will try to briefly summarize it. 
Process in question *_Not fit for purpose vehicle use_* in relation to Fleet markets. 

*Global process:* 
-asking for proof and details from the reporting user 
-informing driver about suspension of their account and asking for details of damage, condition and next steps
-first option CS specialist asking fleet driver if he is going to change the vehicle (if confirmed driver is unblocked)
-another option is if fleet driver confirms that vehicle is fit for use and he will use it, CS specialist asks for proof
-another option if fleet driver confirms that he will wait until vehicle will be repaired, CS specialist does not lift the block and waits for proof 

*Suggested process:*
-asking for proof and details from the reporting user 
-CS specialist is suspending the car and fleet driver is informed about it by auto-comms 
-CS or OPS specialist unblocks the car in case of contact from fleet driver or owner with the proof that condition of the car is sufficient to drive

High-level validation of potential eater & courier fraud based on the sampled orders was done.

*Eater fraud:*

To validate for potential eater fraud, we looked at how many orders were made by unique users within the analysed period of time to see what % of all their orders were reported as “undelivered” & how these unique users distribute per cohorts.

* 44% of unique eaters reported 0%-10% of their orders “undelivered” in the analysed period of time, the average count of orders per unique user in the same period was 30. So we might relatively safely exclude any fraud on this cohort.
* Almost 9% of unique users had reported 90%-100% of their orders “undelivered”. These are either new users, since avg order count per unique user in this cohort is 1, or it's likely fraudulent. 

* Link to validation [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nXHgu1T2EARRNtJ5EZDitX9095uh9-5leze8Uktdo9o/edit#gid=66896812|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nXHgu1T2EARRNtJ5EZDitX9095uh9-5leze8Uktdo9o/edit#gid=66896812|smart-link] 

*Courier fraud:*

To validate for potential courier fraud, we've looked at how many orders that were reported as “undelivered” were associated with the unique couriers. 

* There were no unique couriers who were reported not to deliver more than one order in the analysed period of time. In other words, no repeated reports associated with the same courier.
* Link to validation [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Mr7TfQhoCtogxCjZFHDtEIdX-fkNCEEUklVmMd0CAQw/edit#gid=1953976559|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Mr7TfQhoCtogxCjZFHDtEIdX-fkNCEEUklVmMd0CAQw/edit#gid=1953976559|smart-link]

I spent some time looking at the data to do some power analysis this week.
Here are some thoughts, please take a look and let me know what you think.[Notebook here.|https://bolt-datascience.cloud.databricks.com/?o=3829506390716583#notebook/4100570200891179/command/4100570200891192]*On Power analysis:*At the start, I began doing the power analysis the way we always do:1) Check that the model does not give a False positive on a period when nothing happened

# Add some artificial effect to the data, checking whether it could capture it.So for Azerbaijan, my minimal detectable impact was 50%.

But adding 50% actually means just getting additional 10 woman drivers across the whole [month.At|http://month.At] the same time, if we get 10 additional  women drivers, the effect would be observable with an eye (or with regular period over period comparison), while if we get 2-3, I am not sure we would be eager to strive for a very sensitive test to capture those (this is not exactly the result we’re waiting for from the business side, let me know if I am wrong here).So I am just thinking:Given the sparseness of the data, looks like we are not exactly looking to solve the *problem of uncertainty*. We either see the impact or do not see it. And we might not need Power analysis [http://here.At|http://here.At|smart-link]  the same time, we will just need to compare the uplift (if there’s any) to the counterfactual markets to attempt to solve the *problem of causality* (to make sure that it’s the ads who made the whole impact).*Side Note 1:*
On choosing the predictors:Having checked the article on Causal Impact, we found out that one of the advantages of CausalImpact is that selects the predictors and the weights for you allowing not to care about the interpretability. I am not sure I exactly understand why that is right now, but decided to test the following:For each of the participating markets we take:

* women driver activations as target metric
* women driver activations from other markets as candidates for a counterfactualSo we might want to check women driver activations to women driver activations.The amount of registrations indeed looks very sparse on daily level, but I do not think this is a problem for CausalImpact.Having run the out-of-sample tests on April’s data, it looks like the model is not capturing any impact in April (as expected) for all the countries except:- Nigeria (decrease)
* Portugal (decrease)
* Croatia (increase)
* Lithuania (decrease)And it looks like at least for Croatia and Portugal it’s visible with an eye that something is happening on those markets during April.

*Side Note 2:*
I want to discuss with you for how long we should be controlling the markets.  But I think this deserves a discussion.Thank you!

In Carta there are two different emails in place: portfolio email and contact email. Portfolio email is used for creating an account, logging in and contact email is something that option holder can edit themselves at any point of time, to make sure that they’d always receive any updates. By default 1 email is used in both places.

When granting option units then Bolt uses personal email addresses which are taken from our HR system. That’s why it’s important to make sure that accurate email is added. During your first grant [bolt.eu|http://bolt.eu] email was added under your personal email field in BambooHR (our previous HR system) and that is why this was also used an email when creating and account.

Please see Carta guide on [how to merge your accounts|https://support.carta.com/s/article/merging-portfolios].

Section 7 says:

_For the purposes of the provisions of art. 572.2 of the Civil Procedure Act, it is expressly agreed by the contracting parties that the amount payable in the event of enforcement shall be the amount resulting from the notification made by SC RENTING._

Art. 572 of the Civil Procedure Act refers to the “money execution”, i.e. to the judicial activity of forced execution, the purpose of which is to obtain a certain amount of money from the debtor's assets in order to deliver it to the creditor.

This proceeding is based on an enforceable title which, directly or indirectly, results in a duty to deliver a liquid sum of money (such as invoices, debt securities, etc.). 

On presentation of one of these enforcement title, provided that there is no opposition from the debtor, the judge will declare the existence of the debt and the enforcement of the same for the amount appearing on the enforcement title.

Section 7 would mean that in the event that SC RENTING enforces a debt arising from the contract, the amount for which enforcement would be ordered would be the amount established by SC RENTING in a prior notice to the debtor.

 I find this clause a bit vague. Maybe we can try to push it back.

Should you have any further questions, please do let me know.
